description:
A guard using === or !== does not compile (probed on fz-rs7.4, PR #358, interp and run):

def f(n) when n === 1, do: :a
def f(_), do: :b

error[lower/unsupported]: compiler2 guards cannot call extern fz_op_identical_ii: return Scalar(Bool) is neither a number nor a reference word (runtime:Kernel.fz:1253)

!== fails the same way on fz_op_not_identical_ii (Kernel.fz:1281). Elixir allows both in guards: f(1) is :a and f(1.0) is :b.

Cause: GuardExtern::new (src/dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs) admits integer, float, reference-word and Checked returns; a boolean return is refused. The strict-equality externs return a boolean.

Change: a guard extern may return a boolean, read as the guard's truth value. The receive matcher already has a strict comparison (emit_typed_eq_cmp with Equality::Strict); check whether === in a guard can be that one implementation rather than a second.

Fails before, passes after, three paths, with an Elixir oracle: === and !== in a function-head guard and a receive guard over 1, 1.0, an atom and a list.

Acceptance: full gate green; the 85-probe guard census rows for === and !== match Elixir.
title: === and !== are allowed in a guard
